label.purpose: Meta text: dates, badges, helper captions.

readout.purpose: Every numeric figure representing real quantities (bags, currency, counts); tabular-nums.

shadows.name: resting-lift
shadows.purpose: Default state for cards and primary buttons.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: Active/pressed state; paired with translateY(1px) instead of a shadow.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single most important action on screen (submit, save, sync retry).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #9C6B2E; color: #FFFFFF; padding: 12px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font: 600 1rem system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(31,27,22,0.08); transition: background 0.15s ease-out, transform 0.08s ease-out, box-shadow 0.08s ease-out; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #7D551F; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A lower-weight action alongside a primary one (cancel, correct).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #FFFFFF; color: #7D551F; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1.5px solid #D9D4CB; border-radius: 6px; font: 600 0.9rem system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #7D551F; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { color: #9C8F80; border-color: #D9D4CB; cursor: default; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Bordered field for form entry; focus is a border color shift, no glow ring.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #FFFFFF; color: #1F1B16; border: 1.5px solid #D9D4CB; border-radius: 4px; padding: 10px 12px; font: 400 1rem system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; width: 100%; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #9C6B2E; } .ds-input:invalid:not(:placeholder-shown) { border-color: #B3402A; }

components.name: Entry Card
components.description: One submitted entry in the operator's list, with its readout figures.

narrative.overview:
Eaglenet exists to put a number on the record the instant it's true, the way a mechanical scale commits a weight the moment the needle settles — not an estimate revised later. The system reads as industrial instrumentation, not office software: warm graphite ink on paper-toned surfaces, a single brass accent used the way a dial's needle or a stamped seal is used — sparingly, and only where it means "this is the number that matters." Components are built solid: thicker borders than a typical SaaS card, a slight lift so buttons and inputs feel like physical controls you press rather than flat regions you tap, and numeric values set in a monospace readout face so a column of figures lines up the way it would on a scale's digital display.

This is a deliberate departure from generic dashboard software: no indigo-on-white gradient buttons, no floating soft-shadow cards on a pure white canvas, no rounded-full pills. Eaglenet is a tool bolted to the workflow of weighing and recording rice, used in direct sun on a phone and at a desk in an office — it should look like it belongs in both places.
keyCharacteristics: A single warm brass accent, reserved for primary actions and confirmed states — never decorative.
Warm graphite ink and paper-toned neutrals instead of cool corporate gray-and-blue.
Solid, mechanical component language: visible borders, modest radius, a slight tactile lift.
Numeric data set in a monospace "readout" face wherever a figure is the point.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Brass Dial appears only on the single most important action or state per screen. If two elements compete for brass, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Tabular Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number that represents a real quantity (bags, currency, counts) is set in the Readout face with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Numbers used as ordinary language stay in Body.

rules.name: The Pressable Rule
rules.body: Anything the user taps to commit data (submit, save, sync retry) carries the Resting Lift at rest and the Pressed treatment on :active. Static, non-interactive surfaces stay flat.

dos: Do reserve Brass Dial for exactly one primary action or state per screen.
Do set every real numeric figure in the Readout monospace face with tabular numerals.
Do keep borders at 1.5px and radius at 4-8px — never a pill shape, never borderless flat cards.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color (indigo, blue, teal) alongside Brass Dial.
Don't use soft, diffuse "floating card" shadows — the Resting Lift is small and tight, not a SaaS ambient glow.
Don't set numeric data in the body/UI font — it breaks the "mechanical readout" character.
